text:
kai: Quick design thread: we9re hitting a snag where query batching in the console interacts badly with authz checks. batching coalescer merges 12 small queries into 1 request -> but authz is per-principal-per-entity and can differ. need to decide interface boundary.

:tess: can you sketch the problem with an example?

kai: sure. renderer sends 12 cell reads for tenant A (same user) but different entity ids. coalescer batches to reduce RPCs. central authz can evaluate bulk: allow(entity_ids=[1,2,3]) -> cheaper. but for mixed-tenant or mixed-user flows the batch must be split. the coalescer currently doesn't know authz context, so we either: 1) check authz per-item before batching (more checks), 2) batch then verify/mask results (post-filtering), or 3) attach a decision token from PDP that lets batched backend filter fast.

li: tradeoffs: (1) increases authz qps by N, losing batching benefits. (2) requires backend to apply masks which couples rendering and data services to policy model. (3) token approach needs PDP to return a compact bitmap or predicate token and backend must be able to apply it securely.

priya: important constraint: we cannot leak entity ids or values across tenant boundaries during coalescing. any batching that mixes tenants is forbidden by policy. so coalescer needs to be tenant-aware.

jun: how about a cooperator pattern: coalescer groups only by tenant and principal, then attaches a schema: {tenant, principal, intent_hash}. backend exposes apply_intent(intent_hash, results) endpoint and PDP signs the intent. signature validated by backend. avoids per-item PDP calls.

kai: intent token idea sounds promising. but signing increases PDP complexity and we need revocation semantics if policy changes. also auditability: we must log who/what evaluated.

li: revocation: we can include a short TTL on tokens (e.g., 15s) and include policy_version_id. If token expired or version mismatch backend falls back to per-item check or rejects.

priya: audit: token should carry opaque metadata (policy_version, evaluation_id) that backend logs. sampling for enterprise customers.

:tess: performance concern: token generation adds PDP latency to the fast-path. where does it live? sidecar? central PDP?

kai: options: 1) sidecar issues tokens from local PDP instance (fast, per-pod cache), 2) central PDP issues tokens but we add a caching layer. Sidecar seems logical because coalescer runs near renderer and already co-locates.

jun: also consider hybrid: coalescer asks sidecar for token; sidecar either returns cached token or requests central PDP async and returns a provisional token that marks results as "tentative" until confirmation. backend would need to treat tentative results carefully though. complexity rises.

li: another simple alternative: enrich batch key with authz attributes before batching (principal, role-set, resource-attrs). That reduces token work but increases batch cardinality and may reduce batching efficiency. we should quantify the loss.

priya: suggestion for experiments: simulate realistic dashboard traffic and measure batching efficiency vs authz overhead across three patterns: pre-check-per-item, token-per-batch, enriched-key batching. measure end-to-end render p95 and authz_p95.

kai: agreed. SLO targets: render p95 < 120ms, authz component p95 < 12ms, fallback/miss rate < 1%.

:tess: can we do an A/B in staging with 5k req/s for 30 minutes? li, can you own the traffic sim?

li: yes. will spin up scenarios: single-tenant dense dashboard, mixed-tenant table view, and tenant-heavy with many entities. will output: batch_size_dist, coalesce_rate, authz_qps, p50/p95/p99 latencies.

jun: infra thoughts: token signing requires key mgmt + rotation. we can reuse existing KMS + short-lived keys. try to avoid HSM per token.

priya: also need to consider correctness tests: authz fuzz tests that ensure no leakage when batching happens. product will create a small corpus of edge cases.

:tess: rollout plan sketch: 1) lab prototyping with token and enriched-key locally; 2) staging A/B at 5k rps for 24h; 3) pilot on non-customer dashboards 2% for 48h; 4) gradual ramp with metric gates (render_p95, authz_p95, error_rate). rollback if any metric regresses >5%.

kai: ownership: eng-platform will implement coalescer tenant-aware grouping + token hook; infra builds token signer and key rotation; li runs sims and gathers perf matrix; priya owns tests and audit hooks.

infra-bot: ci/status: coalescer branch builds: rwd/coalescer:sha256:ef12dead. token signer PoC image pushed: rwd/pdptoken-signer:sha256:beefc0de.

li: quick config snippet for intent token TTL we9ll test: ```
intent_token:
  ttl_seconds: 15
  max_batch_entities: 100
  require_signed: true
```

:tess: good. final note: ensure the coalescer emits telemetry per-batch: tenant, principal_hash, batch_size, token_used, backend_masking_time. helps debug regressions.

kai: ok we9ll run the three experiments this week and reconvene. I9ll update the design doc with tokens + enriched-key alternatives. thanks all. :rocket:
